chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Asadi from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi from Aban ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is disliked to recite Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad in one breath.'

key_terms.بِنَفَسٍ وَاحِدٍ: In one breath - Referring to the physical act of reciting the verses without pausing to inhale, which is the subject of the ruling.
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad - The opening phrase of Surah Al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112 of the Quran), often used to represent the entire chapter in this context.
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a juristic ruling indicating a recommended act of omission or a discouraged act of commission, though not forbidden.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas in one breath?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas in a single breath, emphasizing the virtue of *tarteel* (measured, clear recitation) to ensure proper articulation and contemplation. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the aesthetic and spiritual quality of recitation, ensuring that even the shortest chapters are recited with the dignity and presence of heart befitting the declaration of Divine Unity.
